x_axis.name: AI-Native Workflow Automation
x_axis.description: How much of the day-to-day bookkeeping workflow (categorization, reconciliation, close) is handled automatically without manual data entry
x_axis.rationale: Acmecorp's core differentiation claim is automated bookkeeping via AI; this axis directly tests that claim against incumbents' recently-added AI features and against Pilot's human-powered automation.

y_axis.name: Installed Base / Distribution Reach
y_axis.description: Size and reach of the current customer base and distribution channel (accountant ecosystem, direct, etc.)
y_axis.rationale: Distribution reach is the table-stakes dimension incumbents dominate; pairing it with automation depth shows whether Acmecorp's product edge is offset by a distribution disadvantage.

points.x_evidence: AI-assisted categorization covers ~70% of transactions automatically at launch, positioned as the core product wedge.
points.y_evidence: 300 customers, 9 months live — limited installed base and no accountant-channel distribution yet.

points.x_evidence: New AI categorization feature launched 2025-09 but layered onto an otherwise manual-entry-heavy legacy workflow.
points.y_evidence: Largest SMB accounting install base by a wide margin, decades of accountant-channel distribution.

points.x_evidence: Bank-feed reconciliation is strong but categorization automation is comparable to QuickBooks, not more advanced.
points.y_evidence: Large international installed base, weaker specifically in the US.

points.x_evidence: Invoicing-first tool; minimal automated bookkeeping categorization beyond basic rules.
points.y_evidence: Meaningful base among freelancers but far smaller than the two leaders and not the same buyer segment.

points.x_evidence: High automation of outcomes, but achieved via a human bookkeeping team layered on software rather than pure AI automation.
points.y_evidence: Reaches a meaningful slice of VC-backed startups but a much smaller addressable base than SMB-wide players.

points.x_evidence: No automation by definition — a spreadsheet plus a human bookkeeper.
points.y_evidence: Still the most common approach among very early-stage SMBs, so nominal 'installed base' is large but diffuse and unbranded.

differentiation_claims.claim: AI-powered bookkeeping automates 70%+ of transaction categorization with no manual rules setup
differentiation_claims.evidence: Founder-reported figure from internal product metrics; QuickBooks' comparable AI categorization feature (launched 2025-09) has not published an equivalent automation-rate figure, so no independent competitor benchmark exists.
differentiation_claims.challenge: 70% is self-reported and unaudited. What's the false-categorization rate, and how was 70% measured — all transactions, or only ones the model had prior training exposure to?

differentiation_claims.claim: Cuts SMB bookkeeping time by 80% versus manual methods
differentiation_claims.evidence: Consistent directionally with the AI-categorization claim and with the reported 18% MoM growth, but no time-motion study or customer-reported before/after benchmark was provided.
differentiation_claims.challenge: 80% is a strong, specific number with no independent measurement behind it. Can you show a time-tracked before/after case study from an actual customer?

differentiation_claims.claim: Differentiated from QuickBooks/Xero because they are legacy manual-entry tools
differentiation_claims.evidence: QuickBooks shipped an AI-assisted categorization feature in September 2025 across all tiers — the 'legacy manual-entry' framing is now dated by roughly 8 months as of this analysis.
differentiation_claims.challenge: QuickBooks has already shipped a comparable AI feature. What is the actual gap between your categorization accuracy/coverage and theirs, rather than the binary 'they're manual, we're not' framing?
